answer: A credit-network protocol resists Sybil attacks by routing interactions through a bounded trust trellis. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of acquiring authentic bilateral credit lines per identity, as fake clusters cannot widen flow capacity through honest network bottlenecks. Whether an agent executes a data voyage or trades tokenized jade, interactions remain capped by organic peer endorsements. However, this design imposes severe cold-start friction on legitimate new participants.
